主要内容: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers increased by 1.8 percent from November 2011 to November 2012. This reflects a 12-month percent change in the CPI, with the overall index rising by 1.8 percent. The medical care index saw the highest increase at 3.4 percent, followed by shelter and transportation services, both rising by 2.2 percent. The food index also increased by 1.8 percent, while the energy index rose by 0.3 percent. In contrast, the index for used cars and trucks fell by 2.3 percent over the year. These data are provided by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) as part of its Consumer Price Index program. The report highlights the inflationary trends across various sectors during this period.
